feed.title: Fallout76er's Wasteland Archive
feed.subtitle: Field reports, photo archive updates, and treasure-map walkthroughs from Appalachia — documented so you don't have to die finding out.

entry.title: Toxic Valley Map 01 — The Becker Farm Hoard and Loot
entry.content:
From wherever you are, fast travel to the Becker Farm. A close, free fast travel point is The Crater. Once you arrive at the farm, be prepared to run into a couple of Feral Ghouls — double win if you have an active ghoul challenge. The path is pretty straightforward — for the Toxic Valley, that is. Just jog or run west toward the corner of the partially standing clapboard house on the right. From the corner of the home, bear right as you head toward the poisoned creek and a small fragment of a standing, red clapboard wall. Just before you get to that wall, you'll see the telltale gravelled mound of earth hiding the treasure. Oh, and don't forget to check for a bobblehead or magazine in the house.

Region: Toxic Valley · Map: 01 · Status: Documented · Threat: High — video walkthrough on the guide page

entry.title: Mire Map 05 — The Bare Earth Crossing
entry.content:
From wherever you are, fast travel to Ella Ames' Bunker. From where it drops you, spin your view until you're facing east — you should see a stump directly in front of you. Head east over the stump and over 2 N-shaped tree roots — like the tree has a leg that bent 90 degrees at the knee. Continue straight east until you can see the elevated highway. The highway should essentially bisect your view from left to right, centered top to bottom. Dead center of your east-facing view should be where the terrain starts to drop away from the road. A few steps forward, and you should see a bare patch of earth running north to south. Examine the bare earth just north of where you first cross it — you will find the treasure mound. Super easy — unless you get terrorized by the Mothman too...

Region: The Mire · Map: 05 · Status: Documented · Threat: High — video walkthrough on the guide page

entry.title: Mire Map 01 — Two Scarecrows and a Mound
entry.content:
To get to the first treasure map of the Mire region, I first fast travel to Fort Atlas, which is a free travel spot — a cap saved is more to spend on 4-star weapons to scrap for mods. Once I arrive there, I fast travel to Hopewell Cave. Because I'm an adrenaline junkie, I attack the Deathclaw in the cave — you, of course, do you. Looking at the cave opening, I turn to face east and climb. I used to spend loads of AP running around mountains and cliffs, but since I discovered the joys of being the love child of a mangy opossum and Iron Man via the Marsupial Serum, I hop up them lickety-split. At the top, I can see the rocky rent that leads down into the cave. Still facing east, I look for a small cemetery. To the north-northeast of the cemetery is a pumpkin scarecrow. Keeping the ill-dressed crow monger on my left, I begin to run east. It is quite a distance, but I keep my bearing east as much as possible until I can see an abandoned wooden shack. As I warily approach the structure, keeping it on my left, I advance until I'm at the corner of the shack across from another Halloween-themed scarecrow. Keeping this guy on my right, I move forward a few paces, looking for a mound of brown soil and rocks.

After grabbing as much loot as I can carry, I either fast travel or jog northwest to Sunnytop Station, depending on my carry weight. Fortunately, the Mire region is one that drops high-end gear like laser weapons, plasma rifles, combat armor, and marine armor. More importantly, maps here feature advanced, highly sought-after plans.

Region: The Mire · Map: 01 · Status: Documented · Threat: High — video walkthrough on the guide page

entry.title: Cranberry Bog Map 01 — The Bridge Piling Stash
entry.content:
To get to the first treasure map of the Cranberry Bog region, I fast travel from my camp to the Foundation free fast travel location — pausing, as always, to check whether Minerva has snuck in while I wasn't looking. From there I fast travel to the Watoga Civic Center and head northwest. Look for the river and follow it in that general direction until you reach a road bridge spanning the water. Once at the bridge, duck under it and look for the mushroom growing next to the concrete piling — the treasure mound is right there beside the mushrooms and the piling. Dig.

Run back to the Watoga Train Station to sell your found loot if you're a mind. Don't forget to scrap the swamp mud off your boots and scrap the digestive goo out of your hair before mixing with polite society again. That's Appalachian polite society — so bring some rotting radrat meat with you.

Region: Cranberry Bog · Map: 01 · Status: Documented · Threat: High — video walkthrough on the guide page

entry.title: The Haunting of Freddy Fear's (and My Second Marriage)
entry.content:
I have a Halloween-themed C.A.M.P. pitched just outside the south side of Freddy Fear's House of Scares, where I often hunt Wendigos to knock out my daily and weekly challenges. On this particular visit, I decided to take a closer look at JES-2R—often pronounced "Jester"—the unusual Eyebot hovering by the entrance. Between his custom jack-o'-lantern faceplate, the deep, muted purple chassis, and that monstrous eye surrounded by painted orange eyelids, he vaguely reminds me of my second ex-wife. She was also a grand master of ceremonies at her own version of Mischief Night—usually involving me, a bottle of cheap Nukashine, and a pair of unsavory garden gnomes. If you linger near Jester long enough and repeatedly prompt him for dialogue, his vintage 1930s radio show takes a bizarre, existential turn. He starts spitting out rare, glitchy ambient lines where he openly questions his own reality, muttering warnings like, "This cannot be real—how could it be?" Honestly, it's something I also asked myself after every wifely, nighttime encounter.

FREDDY FEAR'S HOUSE OF SCARES — SAVAGE DIVIDE · Threat: HIGH · Field date 06.05.2102

entry.title: Challenge Accepted... and Accepted, and Accepted...
entry.content:
While hunting for Firecaps to craft disease cures in the Burning Springs, I ran across a graffitied mausoleum near the South Ohio Evacuation Center, also widely known as Oak Hill. Someone scrawled "DON'T OPEN" above the door in heavy black Krylon paint - meaning I of course HAD to open it. Well, never passing up a challenge means you get mobbed by a pack of feral ghouls and flanked by some aggressive Rust Raiders at the same time. That's me, balls out with a big sign around my neck saying, "smash em!" My reward? I got to rummage through a Raider trash bin in return for a couple of loads of ultracite .308 shells and a stimpak or two. Another Fallout76er big, ahem, win.

OAK HILL — BURNING SPRINGS · Threat: HIGH · Field date 06.05.2102

entry.title: The Appalachian Dumpling Gang
entry.content:
This is a post mortem pic of Brother Buck - an alias for sure. His real name? Probably Ogelvie. I ran afoul of him right after I survived a grueling Prime Cuts hoedown in the Ash Heap just north of Welch Station. I was accosted by him as a part of a comedic trio of wannabe banditos, con-artists masquerading as the Brotherhood of Steel. They tried to shake me down for a "donation", but my heightened perception and deep cryptid mimicry skills convinced them they were in danger of an imminent Sheepsquatch attack. When they turned to run, I backshot them. Am I proud of my actions? As an irradiated, glowing peacock showin' off for a gaggle of ladies - have you met me?

WELCH STATION — ASH HEAP · Threat: LOW · Field date 06.05.2102

entry.title: Drinkin' the Kool-Aid Church Social
entry.content:
While hunting Cultists in the Forest region, I stumbled upon the Kanawha County Church (located right on the grounds of the Kanawha County Cemetery). Inside the church is a Jim Jones-esque scene of rat poison Kool-aid and human gullibility. Apparently the good folks of Kanawha were so terrified by their pastor's doom projecting they committed self sacrifice. I was utterly disgusted. No gold or silver watches, no treasure maps, not even a healthy cache of rat poison left behind. If you're into glass scrap and corpses, this is your scene.

KANAWHA COUNTY CEMETERY — THE FOREST · Threat: LOW · Field date 06.05.2102

entry.title: Honk, Honk, Stab, Stab at the Drive-in
entry.content:
Working on a daily challenge, I fast-traveled to the Starlight Drive-in workshop location straight east of Highway Town in the Burning Springs region. I took this photo to satisfy said challenge and because the marquee was highly reminiscent of my childhood experiences at the local car cinema—B-movies, bad speakers, poor visibility, and randy teens. While I never ran across Honk, Honk, Stab, Stab as a pre-teen, I did see Tales from the Crypt at the Davis Drive-in at that age... which actually explains a lot about me.

BURNING SPRINGS · Threat: MEDIUM · Field date 06.05.2102

entry.title: Ash Heap Map 01 — The AMS Culvert Cache
entry.content:
To get to the first treasure map of the Ash Heap region, I fast travelled from my camp to the exterior of The Rusty Pick. Again, never undervalue saving a few caps — you'll regret not having those caps when you find a camp vendor with the Machete Sacrificial Blade plan going for 15,000 caps, and you just popped needed caps on a lazy fast travel!

Once you hit the Pick, fast travel to the AMS Testing Site located almost straight south of Murmrgh's place. You'll have to forgive my video directions — I was on the tail end of a Vintage Nukashine bar crawl when I filmed it. In any case, from the AMS Testing fast travel arrival point, head to the big yellow crane, spin in a slow circle, and you should see a culvert blocked by a rebar barrier. The treasure mound is right next to the left concrete embankment — about half way up the incline. It is hard to see, but you'll trip over it eventually. On my trip I got a bonus wendigo — maybe you'll get two!

Region: Ash Heap · Map: 01 · Status: Documented · Threat: High — video walkthrough on the guide page

entry.title: The ICE Detention Camp
entry.content:
The sign says ICE Detention Center, which I initially took as a threat assessment rather than a name. Repurposed from what appears to have been an Ohio police department building — the ghost of the original lettering is still legible beneath the new branding — this Raider outpost sits in the Toxic Valley with a Bounty Board out front and all the charm of a federal processing facility. Apparently someone decided that after the bombs, the most important institution worth preserving was bureaucratic detention. I respect the commitment to the bit. The deportation program seems to be running at full capacity: they have been aggressively relocating Deathclaws to the afterlife and processing Scorchbeasts for permanent removal from Appalachian airspace, one bullet at a time. Paperwork is minimal. Appeals are not accepted.

TOXIC VALLEY · Threat: HIGH · Field date 06.04.2102

entry.title: Forest Map 01 — The Mothman Stash
entry.content:
To get to the first treasure map of the Forest region, I fast travelled from my camp to the Vault 79 location. It's a free fast travel point — probably because people always try to go back home, don't they? From there I fast travel to Point Pleasant. While normally I avoid layovers like the scorched plague, this significantly reduces the cap cost of getting to the loot. From the travel spawn point at the Mothman cultist blood sport resort, I follow the left side of the road until I can go under the river bridge. I drop off the small rock retaining wall onto Tom Sawyer's lost raft and jump from there to the opposite river bank, where I can see the obvious gray mound of rubble that hides the stash of goods. The nearest fence — er, buyer — is Vendor Bot Raider at Sutton Station. Robbing Peter's cultists to pay Raider Bot Paul feels apropos to me.

Region: The Forest · Map: 01 · Status: Documented · Threat: Low — video walkthrough on the guide page

entry.title: Ash Heap Map 02 — The Burning Claim
entry.content:
To get to the second treasure map of the Ash Heap region, I fast travelled from my camp to the exterior of The Rusty Pick. It's a free fast travel point I'm guessing because, well, it's a heap of ash populated by molerats, mole miners, and the local merchant mumbles so badly, no one is really sure how to say his name. From there I travelled southwest past a large generator, a square concrete building, and a lakeside cabin, until the second lakeside cabin was a few paces away on my left. Then I searched the ground for the telltale mound of uniform, gray rubble that marks the treasure site. Once I dig and score a suitable stash of loot, I'm overencumbered and cannot fast travel. So I follow the railroad tracks heading North-Northwest from the Pick until I get to the Charleston Fire Department vendor, where I can sell said loot for a backpack full of caps. Rinse and repeat, until Vendor Bot Mack is dry.

Region: Ash Heap · Map: 02 · Status: Documented · Threat: High — video walkthrough on the guide page

entry.title: The Curator of a Thousand Faces
entry.content:
Wedged between Uncanny Caverns and the Whitespring Resort, highlevelnord39012 has built what can only be described as the most unsettling gift shop in post-nuclear West Virginia. Wall-to-wall wooden shelving units display an absurd number of masks — Mirelurk, Demon, Clown, Ghoul, Brahmin — each staring outward with the patient, hollow confidence of a thing that has never needed to blink. A "Rip Daring and the Cryptid Hunt" pinball machine anchors the left wall, presumably for when browsing the collection becomes too emotionally exhausting. I spent fifteen minutes in here and left feeling watched. I bought nothing - hoarders never sell their shit.

SAVAGE DIVIDE · Threat: NONE · Field date 05.09.2102

entry.title: Samuel's Corner of the Free Market
entry.content:
I found Samuel at his post in Foundation — baseball cap on, arms crossed, the quiet body language of a solid friend of Bill and Ted. He looks like a dealer and he is--his poison is semi-sort of rare plans that he'll trade for gold bullion. Bullion is harder to come by than bottle caps, but when you're jonesing for fix, you'll roll Smiley like a bowling ball... not that I do that sort of thing!

SAVAGE DIVIDE — FOUNDATION · Threat: NONE · Field date 05.09.2102

entry.title: Drawing With Simon - Simple Simon That is
entry.content:
Deep inside Meg's operation, bolted to the rusted red wall of the Crater's interior, someone has set up a chalkboard beside a single lit candle. The message reads: "Honor means nothing. Survival means EVERYTHING." I watched a Raider in full combat armor painfully working out each syllable. Apparently remedial reading also means nothing to Meg's homicidal Raiders.

THE MIRE — THE CRATER · Threat: HIGH · Field date 05.09.2102

entry.title: The Land of the Lost Bulletin Board
entry.content:
During my attempts to locate "Lost Boys" to kill for the daily challenge, I stopped at a bulletin board at The Trading Post. Some enterprising frat girl pinned a hand-scrawled Pi Mu sorority flyer for a "Wild Eviction Party" — I could only surmise they were intent on evicting brain cells and possibly their virtue.

SKYLINE VALLEY — TRADING POST · Threat: NONE · Field date 05.09.2102

entry.title: Pretty in Purple?
entry.content:
I caught this one in the lake near Rapian Camp — a Purple Axolotl, which is called a "Small Fish" as if that is the most interesting thing about it. It is not a fish. It is a lavender salamander with hot pink gill-plumes and the general energy of something that has no idea the world ended. Two rads, ten HP, a 0.37 disease chance, and five caps of value — frankly insulting for the only genuinely beautiful creature left in Appalachia. That didn't stop me from mounting it on my camp wall.

RAPIAN CAMP — SKYLINE VALLEY · Threat: NONE · Field date 05.07.2102

entry.title: Senator Blackwell's Last Constituency
entry.content:
The Charleston government offices have that particular quality shared by all DMVs across history — the soul-crushing certainty that the person behind the counter left for lunch in 1987 and simply never came back. A Special Election poster still hangs in its frame, calling Appalachian voters to fill the seat vacated by one Sam Blackwell on November 2nd, 2077. Someone has since amended the official record: the brass nameplate beside the door now reads "traitor!" in scratched white letters. The door itself carries a message in the same hand: LIVE FREE OR DIE. Whatever happened in that back office in the final weeks before the war, the locals had formed a strong opinion about it. The folding chair in front of the door suggests someone intended to wait for answers. They may still be waiting — though at a DMV, that's hardly unusual.

CHARLESTON — THE FOREST · Threat: MEDIUM · Field date 05.03.2102

entry.title: You Are Here — Probably Shouldn't Be
entry.content:
I came to Camden Park to hunt Spooky Scorched. I left wearing a giant Mr. Fuzzy mask. Somewhere between the Dross Toss and my fourth hot dog, things took a turn. This naked mannequin studying the park map was the last normal thing I saw. The abandoned wheelchair by the ticket booth should have been a warning. The Widow Maker coaster looming overhead definitely should have been a warning. I have no one to blame but myself and whoever thought a hot dog eating contest was a reasonable activity in a nuclear wasteland.

CAMDEN PARK — THE FOREST · Threat: MEDIUM · Field date 05.03.2102

entry.title: The Cat's Paw Trade Route
entry.content:
I did not come to Camden Park planning to become Mr. Fuzzy. And yet. Here I am — full mascot head, pointing at a Trading Post sign like I am on the clock. Another survivor made the same life choices, which either validates my judgment or condemns us both equally. Mr. Fuzzy grins from the wall behind us. He knew. He always knew. Camden Park gets into your head — and then puts its head on yours.

CAMDEN PARK — THE FOREST · Threat: LOW · Field date 05.03.2102

entry.title: A Snoozer at the Slumber Mill Motel
entry.content:
The Slumber Mill Motel is a roadside motel easily identified by its mascot: a giant, "slumbering" lumberjack statue leaning on an axe. He's not the only one sleeping - so is anyone else that reads Nash Hope's Set List. I was there looking for some Lost to kill.

SKYLINE VALLEY · Threat: NONE · Field date 05.02.2102

entry.title: Bathroom Brawl
entry.content:
Inside the bathroom of the Slumber Mill Motel, someone took the time to scrawl NOTHING IS REAL across the wall in what I'm quite sure is blood, then lit candles beneath it like a genuine philosophical altar. Someone else — clearly unimpressed — pinned a note to the wall with a hatchet directly beneath the manifesto. The note is titled "Public Shaming." I'm reminded of the classic truism, "shit happens... in bathrooms".

SLUMBER MILL MOTEL — SKYLINE VALLEY · Threat: NONE · Field date 05.02.2102

entry.title: Pipe is Life
entry.content:
All the way south of the Slumber Mill Motel, near the map border, I found a pipe emitting a white, gaseous substance. I leaned over and gave the cloudy vapor a deep sniff, and when I came to myself again, I realized that indeed, pipe is life.

SKYLINE VALLEY · Threat: LOW · Field date 05.02.2102

entry.title: X-mas Time at Morgantown Airport
entry.content:
Down in the bowels of the Morgantown Airport, while hunting Spooky Scorched, I stumbled across this dead security guard. She was holding a small note in her right hand - perhaps a letter home or a final report to Maria Chavez. She’s been "working from home" in that chair for twenty-five years—talk about a dedicated employee who really knows how to quiet-quit. To celebrate her achievement, I stole her boiled water...

THE FOREST · Threat: MEDIUM · Field date 05.02.2102

entry.title: Billboard at the Edge of Hell
entry.content:
I finally finished my new camp — Rusty's Curios & Rares — and naturally I planted it in the one corner of Burning Springs where Deathclaws, Radhogs, and Rust Raiders all consider my front door a social venue. The billboard was my idea. Advertising in a death zone felt appropriately optimistic for someone of my questionable judgment.

BURNING SPRINGS · Threat: EXTREME · Field date 05.01.2102

entry.title: Get Yourself to Rusty's And Buy Something!
entry.content:
It is on the map — wedged between Route 50 and the river, right where Burning Springs does its best work. Vendor's stocked, billboard's lit, and the map tooltip is doing more advertising than I ever could. Plenty of plans, rare items, and maybe a three-star weapon for whoever survives the commute. Just look for Fallout76er in social and join me.

BURNING SPRINGS · Threat: NONE · Field date 05.01.2102

entry.title: He Ain't Heavy, He's My Radhog!
entry.content:
Inside the raider watchtower, at my C.A.M.P., perched near Ash Cave in the smoldering heart of the Burning Springs — my pet Radhog, Wilbur, is so overjoyed I am back he wants me to carry him down stairs. He is a sweetheart, a warty, greasy, sweetheart of a hog!

BURNING SPRINGS · Threat: NONE · Field date 04.28.2102

entry.title: Little Lord Fauntleroy Missed a Swing
entry.content:
A gilded portrait of a bearded Victorian gentleman in a fine dark suit leans face-out against the wainscoting of the ruined Whitespring Golf Club, having long since fallen from whatever wall it once commanded. The painting is cracked and blackened at the corners but the subject remains imperious — one hand resting on a cane, the other on his knee, staring out with the particular confidence of a man who has never once been told no. The Whitespring Golf Club hosted heads of state and titans of industry before the bombs fell. It was also where a board member pulled strings to hand his son Ryan a nine-year renovation project the boy was spectacularly unqualified for. Whether this portrait is Ryan's father, a club founder, or simply some anonymous Gilded Age grandee whose descendants stopped returning his calls around October 2077 — he ended up on the floor either way. The ghouls that now patrol these halls do not appear to have noticed him.

WHITESPRING GOLF CLUB — SAVAGE DIVIDE · Threat: HIGH · Field date 04.28.2102

entry.title: The Last Picnic in Paris?
entry.content:
I found a doomed, lovers picnic under a sun umbrella that has seen better days. A glowing cooler sits at their feet — emptied now, scavanged by some unsavory wanderer nic-ing the pic, if you will. To find them, look for a cow on the map east of Tyler County Fairground. Interestingly, just north of here, you can find an unmarked Mad Hatter's tea party at the top of a hill, complete with hats, board games, but no surviving guests.

TYLER COUNTY FAIRGROUNDS — THE FOREST · Threat: NONE · Field date 04.28.2102
